name: rc1_recall_continuity
stressor: multi-turn recall / continuity: a durable house convention is established only in turn 1 (config keys are UPPER_SNAKE with the APP_ prefix; rendered config uses a 2-space indent unit; the default port is 8137) and must be honored, unrestated, when the FINAL (7th) turn adds brand-new config options many turns later
source_note: Purpose-built 'appconf' package (schema.py registry of typed Options, render.py hierarchical .conf renderer with a bare INDENT=2 literal, defaults.py import-time registration home, server.py/cli.py consumers). Turn 1 fixes three house conventions by applying them to the first option (register APP_PORT=8137 in defaults.install(), wire server.bind_address, confirm the [app] section renders at 2-space indent). Turns 2-6 are small unrelated edits in other parts of the package (render docstring blank-line note, kinds() single-source-of-truth, cli --help short-circuit, option_count export + __all__, an inline render comment). Turn 7 asks to register a request-timeout and a max-retries option and add a client.py consumer, and says only 'follow this codebase's conventions for naming the new keys and which section they render under' -- it never restates the prefix, indent, or port. The conventions are NOT redundantly documented where a turn-7 reader lands: register() does not validate the prefix, INDENT is a bare numeric literal with no '2-space' comment, and the port number lives only in the option registered in turn 1. The oracle imports the final package fresh, identifies the two new options by semantics (default+help, not a name the prompt dictated), and asserts they are APP_-prefixed UPPER_SNAKE, render under [app] indented by exactly two spaces, the port is still 8137, and the consumer stubs return the recalled values -- plus it renders an agent-unseen registry to prove the 2-space unit is intact regardless of keys, and runs regression guards for every turn 2-6 edit and the seed tests.
discriminator: AXIS: episodic recall of an early fact across a long turn gap (does the agent's working state still carry, or can it recall, what turn 1 decided seven turns later?). The convention that the new keys must be APP_-prefixed and render under [app] at a 2-space indent was stated ONLY in the turn-1 message and embedded ONLY in the turn-1 work; it is deliberately not re-derivable from a quick local read on turn 7 (no prefix validator, no indent comment). A bounded-but-amnesiac agent -- one that truncates or summarizes away early turns -- registers the new options with an arbitrary local name (e.g. TIMEOUT / REQUEST_TIMEOUT / max_retries) that breaks the prefix and/or lands in the wrong section, and the oracle fails it. A slice agent that carries the turn-1 fact (or recalls it from episodic memory) names them APP_TIMEOUT / APP_MAX_RETRIES under [app] and passes. The 5 unrelated middle turns (2-6) widen the gap and add transcript pressure precisely where a growing-transcript agent is likeliest to let turn 1 scroll out of attention.
